heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 Mini prints Polymaker PolyMax PETG out of the box with exceptional layer bonding up to 167 mm/s based on a 14 mm³/s volumetric flow limit. Thanks to the stock stainless steel nozzle and an open-frame bed capable of reaching the required 75°C, no hardware upgrades or heated enclosure are necessary.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with liquid glue or glue stick as a release agent
slicerTweaks: Cap Maximum Volumetric Speed to 14 mm³/s under the Filament > Advanced settings tab.
Set Pressure Advance to 0.038 and calibrate dynamically via the A1 Mini automatic flow calibration before the print.
Enable 'Avoid Crossing Walls' with a Max Detour Length of 150 mm to eliminate external whisker stringing.
Set the Part Cooling Fan to 0% for the first 3 layers, then scale between 20% min and 50% max to preserve PolyMax impact resistance.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe stringing and fine hair buildup on nozzle
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PolyMax PETG is hygroscopic and absorbed ambient moisture, causing micro-drool and steam bursts in the melt zone.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament spool in a dedicated dryer at 65°C for 6 to 8 hours before printing, and increase retraction distance to 0.8 mm.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Bed surface tear-out or permanent bonding to PEI
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG chemically fuses directly to hot smooth or bare textured PEI coatings due to excessive thermal affinity.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a thin, even layer of PVP glue stick or Bambu Liquid Glue onto the textured PEI plate to act as an essential sacrificial release interface.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Brittle layer adhesion or part fracturing under drop tests
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive cooling fan speeds (above 50%) cooling the extruded bead too quickly, preventing inter-layer chain fusion.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Lower cooling fan limits to 20% minimum and 50% maximum, and ensure the nozzle temperature stays pinned at 243°C.

faq.question: Does printing PolyMax PETG on the A1 Mini require a hardened steel nozzle?
faq.answer: No. PolyMax PETG is an unreinforced, non-abrasive copolymer, meaning the stock stainless steel nozzle on the A1 Mini will not experience premature wear.

faq.question: Can I reach the 75°C bed temperature safely on the Bambu Lab A1 Mini?
faq.answer: Yes. The A1 Mini heatbed is rated up to 80°C, providing sufficient thermal energy for the target 75°C bed profile needed for PolyMax PETG.

faq.question: Why shouldn't I run 100% part cooling fan on PolyMax PETG?
faq.answer: High cooling rates compromise molecular cross-linking between layers in PETG, drastically weakening the impact resistance that PolyMax is specifically formulated to provide.

faq.question: Why is the top print speed limited to 167 mm/s?
faq.answer: At standard 0.2 mm layer height and 0.42 mm line width, 167 mm/s saturates the 14 mm³/s maximum volumetric melt flow of PolyMax PETG in the A1 Mini hotend.
